findings: X1 v2.3 inherits R3 protocol; X1 frozen contract requires explicit source seed or successful separate TECH reset receipt.

reset.py requires exact finite physical/controller state, one-step outcomes and render equality across tested seeds, repeats and official/adapter paths; failed ctrl/warmstart and post-step qpos/qvel satisfy its pre-existing blocking condition.

Pinned Cube.reset accepts seed but sends seed=None to variation reset and omits seed from super().reset; this is a source-level seed propagation defect, not proof that every observed difference has that sole cause.

Official Cube evaluation callables restore only qpos/qvel and target pose; adding control/warmstart restoration or seed forwarding changes the frozen environment/adapter. Equal render pixels do not establish the frozen physical-state equivalence.

Cache, separate128 TECH updates, fixed3x30000 predictor/pred_proj refits and h1/2/5 source-trajectory open-loop evaluation do not require simulator reset fallback and can continue under the original data/model freezes.

Closed-loop performance must remain technically unevaluable rather than algorithm failure or zero success. This conclusion is scoped to the current fixed interface and exact gate; it is not a claim Cube cannot be evaluated under a separately authorized revised protocol.
